why: The GitHub repo contains only three rendered PDFs (PCA_Kmeans.pdf, PCA_Kmeans_Decathlon.pdf, PCA_Kmeans_Iris.pdf) — zero source files, no R/Python scripts, no data, no README. There is nothing to run or port, so the only viable path is to reimplement the paper's method (standardize USArrests -> PCA loadings -> K-means on the transposed standardized matrix with K=2 -> S_{k,j} = sum of absolute loadings, P_{k,j} = S_{k,j}/sum_k S_{k,j}) from the paper and the claim contract. The method is fully specified and the numbers are self-consistent: with prcomp-style loadings |0.536|+|0.583|+|0.278|+|0.543| on PC1, S_{2,PC1} = 0.536+0.583+0.543 = 1.662 and S_{1,PC1} = 0.278, giving P_{2,PC1} = 1.662/1.940 = 0.857, exactly matching C1-C4; PC1/PC2 variance shares (~62%/25%) match standard prcomp on standardized USArrests up to the paper's rounding. The whole target is a 50x4 dataset and a single K-means fit, so no author code is needed.
est_runtime: under 1 minute of command time (a few seconds of actual compute)
blockers: repository ships only PDF renders of the analysis; no executable code at all
original results were produced in R (prcomp + kmeans); Python 3.12 reimplementation must match R's standardization (n-1 sd) and PCA sign convention
PCA loading signs are arbitrary — must compare absolute values as the contract does
K-means on 4 points in 50-dim space is seed/init sensitive; needs multiple starts or fixed init to guarantee the {Murder, Assault, Rape} vs {UrbanPop} split

approach: The GitHub repository contains only PDF renders, so this plan reimplements the paper's USArrests pipeline in Python. Load the four numeric USArrests variables, standardize each with its mean and sample SD (ddof=1), run PCA on the correlation matrix, and keep all four prcomp-style eigenvectors as loadings. Transpose the standardized 50x4 matrix to 4x50, run Euclidean K-means with K=2 on the four variable-points, label the singleton UrbanPop cluster as 1 and the Murder/Assault/Rape cluster as 2, then compute S_{k,j}=sum of absolute loadings and P_{k,j}=S_{k,j}/sum_k S_{k,j}. Write all loadings, S/P matrices, variance shares, cluster assignments, and C1-C8 checks to results/metrics.json; a fixed seed plus an exhaustive 7-partition check removes K-means seed sensitivity.
steps: Run `pip install -r requirements.txt`; confirm numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, and requests import correctly.

Implement src/data.py: try data/usarrests.csv first; otherwise download the Rdatasets USArrests CSV with requests, read it with pandas using the first column as State/index, keep columns Murder, Assault, UrbanPop, Rape, cache to data/usarrests.csv, and validate shape (50,4) with no missing values.

Implement src/method.py: standardize X with pandas/numpy ddof=1; fit sklearn PCA with 4 components; set L = pca.components_.T and La = abs(L); run KMeans(n_clusters=2, init='k-means++', n_init=1000, random_state=123) on Z.T; map labels by the cluster containing UrbanPop; compute S and P for all 4 PCs.

Add an exhaustive partition check for p=4: enumerate the 7 unique nonempty proper two-cluster partitions, compute within-cluster SSE for each, and assert the K-means partition is the global SSE minimum and equals {UrbanPop} vs {Murder,Assault,Rape}.

Implement src/verify.py: check loadings shape (4,4) and orthonormal columns; check P sums to 1 for every PC; check cluster sizes {1,3} with UrbanPop singleton; compare C1-C8 values to targets with relative tolerance 0.1.

Implement reproduce.py: default full run writes results/metrics.json; --smoke uses the first 10 states, K=2 with n_init=10, writes results/smoke_metrics.json, and exits nonzero only if smoke-shape checks fail.
Run `python -m src.data` or the equivalent data-loading command to fetch and cache USArrests; inspect shape, columns, means, and sample SDs before the full run.
Run `python reproduce.py --smoke` and confirm the small data-flow run completes, produces non-NaN loadings/S/P, and P columns sum to 1.
Run `python reproduce.py` on the full 50-state dataset; this is the final run and should write results/metrics.json.

Inspect results/metrics.json: confirm S_{2,PC1}~1.662, S_{1,PC1}~0.278, P_{2,PC1}~0.857, P_{1,PC1}~0.143, PC1~62% variance, PC2~25% variance, Assault PC1 loading~0.583, and UrbanPop PC2 loading~0.873.

If any check fails, debug only the paper-defined steps (ddof=1 standardization, correlation-matrix PCA, absolute eigenvectors, Z.T K-means, label mapping); do not tune thresholds or data to force a match.
smoke_test: Run `python reproduce.py --smoke`: load the first 10 USArrests states, standardize with ddof=1, compute 4 PCA components, run K=2 K-means with n_init=10 on Z.T, compute S and P, and write results/smoke_metrics.json. Assert Z.T shape is (4,10), loadings shape is (4,4), S and P shapes are (2,4), no NaNs are present, and every P column sums to 1. The smoke run does not compare to the paper values and is not used for the final claims.
intermediate_checks: USArrests shape is exactly (50,4) after dropping State; columns are Murder, Assault, UrbanPop, Rape; no missing values.
Approximate dataset moments before scaling: Murder mean~7.788 sd~4.356; Assault mean~170.76 sd~83.338; UrbanPop mean~65.54 sd~14.475; Rape mean~21.232 sd~9.366.

PCA loadings matrix is 4x4; columns are orthonormal within numerical tolerance; explained variance ratios sum to 1.0; PC1 is about 0.620 and PC2 about 0.247, both within 10% relative tolerance of the paper's 62.5% and 25%.
Absolute PC1 loadings are approximately Murder 0.536, Assault 0.583, UrbanPop 0.278, Rape 0.543; absolute UrbanPop PC2 loading is approximately 0.873.

K-means partition has sizes {1,3}; the singleton is UrbanPop and the triple is {Murder, Assault, Rape}; the same partition is the global minimum over all 7 unique K=2 partitions of the four transposed variable-points.

Contribution sanity baseline: S_{2,PC1} should be approximately 1.6625 and S_{1,PC1} approximately 0.2782; P_{2,PC1} approximately 0.8567 and P_{1,PC1} approximately 0.1433; P columns sum to 1 within 1e-12.

Random-partition sanity check: a random 1-vs-3 split should not produce the same S/P pattern, confirming the reported values depend on the K-means variable clustering rather than an arbitrary assignment.
budget_plan: Total budget about 8-10 minutes on CPU: 3-4 minutes for environment setup, pip install, and USArrests download/cache; 1 minute for the smoke test; under 1 minute for the full 50-state PCA plus K-means run; 3-4 minutes for validation, JSON inspection, and final reporting; leave a small buffer for network retry if the Rdatasets download is slow.

import itertools, os
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans

p = os.path.join(os.environ['REPRO_DATA_CACHE'], 'usarrests', 'USArrests.csv')
df = pd.read_csv(p, index_col=0)
X = df[['Murder', 'Assault', 'UrbanPop', 'Rape']].astype(float)
print(X.shape, X.columns.tolist(), X.isna().sum().sum())
print(X.mean())
print(X.std(ddof=1))

Z = (X - X.mean()) / X.std(ddof=1)
pca = PCA(n_components=4, svd_solver='full')
pca.fit(Z.values)
L = pca.components_.T
print('loadings (signed):')
print(pd.DataFrame(L, index=X.columns, columns=['PC1', 'PC2', 'PC3', 'PC4']).round(4))
print('abs:')
print(pd.DataFrame(np.abs(L), index=X.columns, columns=['PC1', 'PC2', 'PC3', 'PC4']).round(4))
print('evr:', pca.explained_variance_ratio_.round(5))

ZT = Z.values.T  # 4 x 50
names = list(X.columns)
# exhaustive 2-partitions (fix first var's cluster to break symmetry)
best = None
for mask in itertools.product([0, 1], repeat=4):
    if mask[0] != 0:
        continue
    if len(set(mask)) < 2:
        continue
    sse = 0.0
    for k in (0, 1):
        idx = [i for i in range(4) if mask[i] == k]
        pts = ZT[idx]
        sse += ((pts - pts.mean(axis=0)) ** 2).sum()
    print(mask, round(sse, 4))
    if best is None or sse < best[1] - 1e-12:
        best = (mask, sse)
print('best partition (exhaustive):', best, [names[i] for i in range(4) if best[0][i] == 0], [names[i] for i in range(4) if best[0][1] == 1])

km = KMeans(n_clusters=2, init='k-means++', n_init=1000, random_state=123)
lab = km.fit_predict(ZT)
print('kmeans labels:', dict(zip(names, lab)), 'inertia', km.inertia_)

# seed sensitivity sweep
labs = {}
for s in range(200):
    k2 = KMeans(n_clusters=2, init='k-means++', n_init=10, random_state=s).fit_predict(ZT)
    labs[tuple(k2)] = labs.get(tuple(k2), 0) + 1
print('label patterns over 200 seeds:', labs)

"""The PCA + K-means-on-transposed-data method of arXiv:2512.00979.

Pipeline (Algorithm 1 of the paper, pages 3-4):

  1. Standardize each variable with its mean and *sample* standard deviation
     (n-1 denominator) -> Z                                   [R1]
  2. PCA on Z; loadings matrix L (eigenvectors, prcomp-style)  [R2, R14]
  3. La = |L|, the absolute-loading matrix                     [R3, R13]
  4. ZT = Z^T (p x n): variables become observations           [R4]
  5. Euclidean K-means on ZT with a fixed seed, K = 2          [R5, R6, R12]
  6. S[k, j] = sum_{i in C_k} La[i, j]                         [R8]
  7. P[k, j] = S[k, j] / sum_r S[r, j]                         [R9, R10]

Everything is computed from the data; nothing is read off the paper's tables.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Step 1: standardization (R1)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def standardize(X: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[np.ndarray, dict]:
    """z_ij = (x_ij - mean_j) / sd_j with sd using ddof = 1 (R's `scale`)."""
    A = X.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    mu = A.mean(axis=0)
    sd = A.std(axis=0, ddof=1)
    if np.any(sd <= 0):
        raise ValueError("a variable has zero variance; cannot standardize")
    Z = (A - mu) / sd
    return Z, {"mean": mu, "sd_ddof1": sd}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Steps 2-3: PCA and absolute loadings (R2, R3, R13, R14)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def pca_loadings(Z: np.ndarray, n_components: int | None = None) -> dict:
    """PCA on the standardized matrix; returns prcomp-style loadings.

    ``loadings`` rows are variables, columns are principal components, i.e.
    ``L = pca.components_.T`` so that ``Y = Z @ L`` (paper: Y = ZL).
    """
    n, p = Z.shape
    n_components = p if n_components is None else min(n_components, p)
    model = PCA(n_components=n_components, svd_solver="full")
    model.fit(Z)
    L = model.components_.T                       # (p, n_components)
    evr = model.explained_variance_ratio_          # sums to 1.0
    return {
        "loadings": L,
        "abs_loadings": np.abs(L),                 # La
        "explained_variance_ratio": evr,
        "explained_variance_pct": 100.0 * evr,
        "eigenvalues": model.explained_variance_,  # == correlation eigenvalues
        "n_components": n_components,
        "scores": model.transform(Z),
    }


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Steps 4-5: transpose + K-means (R4, R5, R6, R7, R12)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def kmeans_on_transposed(Z: np.ndarray, k: int, seed: int = 123, n_init: int = 1000) -> dict:
    """Euclidean K-means on ZT = Z.T (variables as observations)."""
    ZT = Z.T                                        # (p, n)  [R4]
    km = KMeans(n_clusters=k, init="k-means++", n_init=n_init, random_state=seed)
    labels = km.fit_predict(ZT)
    return {"labels": np.asarray(labels), "inertia": float(km.inertia_), "ZT": ZT,
            "centroids": km.cluster_centers_, "seed": seed, "n_init": n_init}


def exhaustive_two_partitions(ZT: np.ndarray) -> list[dict]:
    """All 7 unique non-empty proper 2-cluster partitions of 4 points + their SSE.

    Used as a seed-free sanity check: the K-means answer must be the global
    minimum of the K-means objective (Section III.D), so it cannot depend on
    the random seed for this problem size.
    """
    p = ZT.shape[0]
    out = []
    for mask in itertools.product((0, 1), repeat=p):
        if mask[0] != 0 or len(set(mask)) < 2:      # fix symmetry / drop trivial
            continue
        sse = 0.0
        for cl in (0, 1):
            pts = ZT[[i for i in range(p) if mask[i] == cl]]
            sse += float(((pts - pts.mean(axis=0)) ** 2).sum())
        out.append({"mask": mask, "sse": sse})
    return sorted(out, key=lambda d: d["sse"])


def elbow_curve(Z: np.ndarray, k_max: int | None = None, seed: int = 123) -> list[dict]:
    """Within-cluster SSE for K = 1..k_max on ZT (supports the paper's elbow, R5)."""
    ZT = Z.T
    p = ZT.shape[0]
    k_max = p if k_max is None else min(k_max, p)
    curve = []
    for k in range(1, k_max + 1):
        if k == 1:
            sse = float(((ZT - ZT.mean(axis=0)) ** 2).sum())
        else:
            sse = KMeans(n_clusters=k, init="k-means++", n_init=100,
                         random_state=seed).fit(ZT).inertia_
        curve.append({"k": k, "sse": float(sse)})
    return curve


def map_cluster_labels(labels: np.ndarray, names: list[str],
                       cluster_1_members: list[str] | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
    """Renumber raw K-means labels so that cluster 1 / 2 match Table IV (R7).

    The paper fixes the naming: for USArrests, C1 = {UrbanPop} and
    C2 = {Murder, Assault, Rape}.  When ``cluster_1_members`` is given the
    cluster containing those variables becomes 1; otherwise clusters are
    numbered by the first variable (in dataset column order) that appears.
    """
    labels = np.asarray(labels)
    uniq = sorted(set(int(x) for x in labels))
    if cluster_1_members:
        anchor = next(i for i, nm in enumerate(names) if nm in cluster_1_members)
        first = int(labels[anchor])
        rest = [u for u in uniq if u != first]
        order = [first] + rest
    else:
        seen: list[int] = []
        for lab in labels:
            if int(lab) not in seen:
                seen.append(int(lab))
        order = seen
    remap = {raw: idx + 1 for idx, raw in enumerate(order)}
    return np.array([remap[int(x)] for x in labels])

* claim      - the eight contract values (C1-C8) compared with a 10 % relative

"""

    "C4": ("Cluster 1 proportion of contribution to PC1, P_{1,PC1}",

    "C7": ("|loading| of Assault on PC1", "Table II", 0.583, "L_Assault_PC1"),
    "C8": ("|loading| of UrbanPop on PC2", "Table II", 0.873, "L_UrbanPop_PC2"),
}


def extract_values(res) -> dict:
    """Pull the claim-relevant numbers out of a PipelineResult (all computed)."""
    L = res.pca["abs_loadings"]
    vi = {nm: i for i, nm in enumerate(res.variables)}
    ci = {k: i for i, k in enumerate(res.cluster_ids)}
    return {
        "S_C1_PC1": float(res.S[ci[1], 0]),
        "S_C2_PC1": float(res.S[ci[2], 0]),
        "P_C1_PC1": float(res.P[ci[1], 0]),
        "P_C2_PC1": float(res.P[ci[2], 0]),
        "EVR_PC1_pct": float(res.pca["explained_variance_pct"][0]),
        "EVR_PC2_pct": float(res.pca["explained_variance_pct"][1]),
        "L_Assault_PC1": float(L[vi["Assault"], 0]),
        "L_UrbanPop_PC2": float(L[vi["UrbanPop"], 1]),

    """Return a list of {name, passed, detail} structural checks."""
    out: list[dict] = []

    def add(name: str, passed: bool, detail: str = "") -> None:

    Z, L, La = res.Z, res.pca["loadings"], res.pca["abs_loadings"]
    n, p = Z.shape
    add("Z shape (n, p)", Z.shape == (n, p), f"{Z.shape}")
    add("Z columns are standardized (mean~0, sd~1)",
        np.allclose(Z.mean(axis=0), 0, atol=1e-12) and np.allclose(Z.std(axis=0, ddof=1), 1, atol=1e-12),
        f"means={np.round(Z.mean(axis=0), 12).tolist()} sds={np.round(Z.std(axis=0, ddof=1), 12).tolist()}")
    add("loadings shape (p, p)", L.shape == (p, p), f"{L.shape}")
    add("loadings columns orthonormal", np.allclose(L.T @ L, np.eye(p), atol=1e-8),
        f"max|L^T L - I| = {np.abs(L.T @ L - np.eye(p)).max():.2e}")
    add("abs loadings == |loadings|", np.array_equal(La, np.abs(L)), "R3/R13")
    evr = res.pca["explained_variance_ratio"]
    add("explained variance ratios sum to 1", abs(float(evr.sum()) - 1.0) < 1e-10, f"sum={float(evr.sum()):.12f}")
    add("eigenvalues descending", bool(np.all(np.diff(evr) <= 1e-12)), np.round(evr, 6).tolist().__repr__())

    # K-means partition validity (R6, R7)
    sizes = sorted(int((res.cluster_ids == c).sum()) for c in res.cluster_ids)

    if expected_partition is not None:
